findings:
🟠 [e2e-claim-path-not-exercised] MUST-FIX The spec requires the e2e follow-up to call `claimCampaignGeneration({resume:true})` and assert `resume_candidate !== null`; the diff instead calls `intake.verifyResumeCandidate({projection,...})` directly and labels the assertion as if the claim path were tested. The actual acceptance surface (claim records `resume_candidate` for the generation after journal replay) is unproven and the assert message misreports what ran. Remediation: replace the direct verify call with the claim call and assert on its `resume_candidate` (keep the commit equality check).
🟠 [fabricated-writer-fence] MUST-FIX `boundaryGitCandidate` synthesizes a writer fence when `mutation.writer_fence` is absent: `status:'closed'`, `evidence_mode:'dispatch_exit'`, `exit_status:1`, `campaign_id: input.rootRunId`, with a self-consistent `receipt_digest`. None of that closure evidence was observed; it exists only to make `verifyResumeCandidate` pass, which bypasses the "do not weaken" guard by forging its input and duplicates `createWriterFence` contrary to this file's own header rule. Impact: an unfenced (possibly still-writing) candidate becomes resumable, and the fence carries the root run id rather than the campaign id. Remediation: build the fence via `createWriterFence` from `campaign-verification` with the real dispatch result, or return null (no candidate, honest message) when no fence exists.
🟡 [reducer-transition-unpinned] MUST-FIX `reduceCampaignState` now accepts `vertical_verified` directly from `BOUNDARY_REJECTED` (a new transition beyond "accept and preserve git_candidate"), but no test in the diff exercises it: the engine green case stubs `campaignEventAppender`, so the real journal never sees the resume. The GREEN claim "runs verification/review" against the durable journal is therefore unproven. Remediation: add a pin in `implementation-campaign-state-boundary.test.sh` that BOUNDARY_REJECTED + `vertical_verified` advances to REVIEWING and that the pre-existing refusals from other phases are unchanged (or route the resume through the same event AWAITING_DISPOSITION uses).
🟡 [red-case-not-a-resume] MUST-FIX The red engine case never passes `resume: true`, yet its assertion reads "no-candidate BOUNDARY_REJECTED resume is blocked"; the new `boundaryRejectedNoCandidate` early return also fires on non-resume dispatches. The spec's item 1 is a resume. Remediation: add `resume: true` to the red `runImplementationReviewLoop` call so the assertion covers the path it names.
🟡 [stray-semicolon-drop] MUST-FIX `src/engine/autopilot-engine.js` (and mirror) changes the `rejection` object literal terminator from `};` to `}`; valid only via ASI and unrelated to the feature. Remediation: restore `};`.
🔵 [next-action-prose-token] CUT/FOLLOW-UP `next_action` in the persisted controller changes from the machine token `await_boundary_disposition` to the prose sentence "no candidate — re-dispatch is a new attempt" (with an em-dash). If any consumer switches on `next_action`, this breaks it; a safer shape is a token such as `redispatch_new_attempt` plus a separate `message`. Excluded because no consumer breakage is demonstrated in scope.
🔵 [journal-events-dup-push] CUT/FOLLOW-UP The fake `campaignEventAppender` pushes each `eventType` twice through a branch whose both arms are identical; harmless for the `includes` check, but dead code worth collapsing.
